newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela opens Banco Latino fin'l data to bidders.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela opens Banco Latino fin'l data to bidders.

text.p: The Venezuelan government took a first step Monday toward the sale of Banco Latino by opening its financial data to interested bidders, the bank said.

Banco Latino, whose collapse in January 1994 sparked an unprecedented, two-year crisis in the banking sector, plans to complete its privatization by December 15. The bank's board of directors said in a statement published in the local press that "from today the institution enters the final phase of its privatization."

The process started today with the opening of the "data room" of leasing company Arfinan, the statement said. The data room contains information on the bank's financial statements and structure. Part of the Latino group, Arfinan will be converted into a commercial bank with initial capital of 1.2 billion bolivars ($2.6 million). Banco Latino as an entity will disappear.
The auction will include Banco Latino's remaining 46 branches, five drive-in banks, an automatic teller network and deposits of some 135 billion bolivars ($282 million) from nearly 400,000 clients.
Banco Latino President Rolando Salcedo said in September the auction price could be about $78 million.

The opening of the bank's financial statements was held in spite of it being a bank holiday in Venezuela. Many large businesses are remaining open due to their interest in the privatization and in the upcoming sale of CANTV shares as well.
Banco Latino's sale forms part of a privatization program which includes Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado, which the government also took over in 1994.
